lines.en: In 2016, a group of researchers— oh, a new photo.
lines.zh: 二〇一六年，一群研究者——哦，来了张新照片。

lines.en: These researchers set out to measure— did I get that email?
lines.zh: 这些研究者打算去测量——我收到那封邮件了吗？

lines.en: They measured— what was that?
lines.zh: 他们测量的是——那是什么声音？

lines.en: Sorry.
lines.zh: 抱歉。

lines.en: The researchers set out to measure the length of, well, our attention spans.
lines.zh: 研究者要测量的，是我们注意力能持续多久。

lines.en: Participants downloaded a program that tracked how long they stayed focused on a single computer application before switching to another.
lines.zh: 参与者下载了一个程序，记录他们在切换到别的东西之前，能盯着同一个电脑应用看多久。

lines.en: On average, users stuck with a single task for 40 seconds, down from 75 seconds, measured just five years earlier.
lines.zh: 平均下来，用户在同一个任务上停留 40 秒，而仅仅五年前测出的数字还是 75 秒。

lines.en: This doesn’t necessarily mean our attention spans are fundamentally getting shorter.
lines.zh: 这倒不一定说明我们的注意力从根本上变短了。

lines.en: Rather, in today’s world, our attention is being pulled in more directions than ever before.
lines.zh: 更准确地说，在今天这个世界里，我们的注意力被拉向的方向，比以往任何时候都多。

lines.en: This can make finding focus— for work, school, and even the things we love— feel almost impossible.
lines.zh: 这让「找到专注状态」——为了工作、为了学业，甚至为了我们热爱的事——感觉几乎不可能做到。

lines.en: Thankfully, there are ways we can improve and better protect our attention spans, both online and off.
lines.zh: 好在，还是有办法改善并更好地保护我们的注意力，不管是在网上还是离线。

lines.en: Our brains are constantly receiving a flood of information, from sensory input to environmental cues to internal thoughts.
lines.zh: 我们的大脑时刻都在接收潮水般的信息——从感官输入，到环境线索，再到自己心里的念头。

lines.en: Filtering through it all relies on several brain regions.
lines.zh: 要从这些信息里筛选出该看什么，靠的是几个不同的脑区。

lines.en: The prefrontal cortex helps us decide what to pay attention to, while the parietal cortex shines a mental flashlight on that prioritized stream of information while ignoring the rest.
lines.zh: 前额叶皮质帮我们决定该关注什么；顶叶皮质则像打出一束心理上的手电光，照亮那条被优先处理的信息流，同时忽略其余部分。

lines.en: The challenge of sustained attention is keeping that flashlight focused in one place.
lines.zh: 保持持续注意的难点就在于：让这束光始终照在同一个地方。

lines.en: The brain is continuously monitoring all these competing signals.
lines.zh: 大脑在持续不断地监控着所有这些互相竞争的信号。

lines.en: And it redirects your focus if anything is flagged as particularly novel, unexpected, or emotionally charged— whether it’s a knock on the door, a notification, or even a passing thought.
lines.zh: 一旦有什么被标记为格外新奇、出乎意料或者带着情绪，它就会把你的注意力重新引导过去——不论那是敲门声、一条通知，甚至只是一个一闪而过的念头。

lines.en: This ability to constantly scan our environments and quickly refocus was key for human survival.
lines.zh: 这种不断扫描环境、并迅速重新聚焦的能力，对人类生存至关重要。

lines.en: So, while frustrating, getting distracted is inevitable.
lines.zh: 所以，虽然让人恼火，但走神是不可避免的。

lines.en: And our baseline ability to manage distractions can vary based on factors like genetics and brain differences.
lines.zh: 而我们应对干扰的基线能力，会因基因和大脑差异等因素而各不相同。

lines.en: But no matter your starting point, there are ways to improve your ability to stay focused.
lines.zh: 但不管起点在哪里，都有办法提升专注的能力。

lines.en: First, tasks that appropriately challenge you tend to hold your attention best.
lines.zh: 首先，难度正好能挑战到你的任务，往往最能抓住你的注意力。

lines.en: For example, you might focus better when working on a more difficult, intricately patterned puzzle than an easier one.
lines.zh: 举例来说，比起一幅简单的拼图，你在拼那种图案复杂、难度更高的拼图时，可能反倒更专心。

lines.en: Of course, we don’t always have a choice in what needs to get done.
lines.zh: 当然，需要做什么，我们并不总能自己挑。

lines.en: In these situations, it’s helpful to remember that if focusing feels like work, that's because it is.
lines.zh: 在这种情况下，记住一件事会有帮助：如果保持专注让你感觉像在干活，那是因为它本来就是在干活。

lines.en: In fact, some researchers theorize that attention is a limited resource.
lines.zh: 事实上，一些研究者提出，注意力是一种有限的资源。

lines.en: When you start focusing on something, this resource is at its highest, but it depletes over time, leading to more mistakes and increasing the chance you’ll be distracted.
lines.zh: 当你刚开始专注于某件事时，这份资源处于最高点，但它会随时间消耗，导致失误增多，也让走神的概率变大。

lines.en: Multitasking only increases the demand for this resource, exhausting attentional stores more quickly.
lines.zh: 多任务处理只会加大对这份资源的需求，让注意力的储备更快耗尽。

lines.en: That's why focusing on one task and intentionally building in breaks can be helpful.
lines.zh: 正因如此，只专注一件事、并有意识地安排休息，会很有帮助。

lines.en: Studies even show a momentary break, to get a snack or just zone out, can reset this attentional resource.
lines.zh: 研究甚至表明，哪怕是短暂地歇一下——去拿点零食，或者干脆放空一会儿——也能让这份注意力资源重置。

lines.en: And this strategy may be extra beneficial when studying or practicing a new skill.
lines.zh: 这个策略在学习或练习一项新技能时，可能格外有益。

lines.en: During breaks, our minds replay the neural activity patterns of what you just learned, helping to solidify the memory for the long term.
lines.zh: 在休息期间，我们的大脑会重放刚刚学到的内容所对应的神经活动模式，这有助于把记忆长期固定下来。

lines.en: Speaking of studying, stress, sleepiness, and poor mood can all weaken our ability to block out distractions.
lines.zh: 说到学习，压力、困倦和糟糕的情绪，都会削弱我们屏蔽干扰的能力。

lines.en: So activities that reduce stress, like exercising, chatting with friends, or getting a good night’s sleep, also make it easier to stay focused.
lines.zh: 所以那些能减轻压力的活动——比如锻炼、跟朋友聊天，或者好好睡一觉——也会让你更容易保持专注。

lines.en: And nature may offer an extra boost.
lines.zh: 而大自然可能还能再加一把力。

lines.en: In one study, a 15-minute walk outdoors led to greater improvements in lab-based attention tasks than the same walk indoors.
lines.zh: 在一项研究中，到户外散步 15 分钟，比在室内走同样长的时间，能让参与者在实验室注意力任务上的表现提升得更多。

lines.en: Another effective strategy is mindfulness meditation.
lines.zh: 另一个有效的策略是正念冥想。

lines.en: This practice is all about staying in the present moment through exercises like spending 12 minutes focusing on the sensations of breathing, which can help train your attention over time.
lines.zh: 这种练习的核心是活在当下，比如花 12 分钟把注意力放在呼吸的感觉上——久而久之，这有助于训练你的注意力。

lines.en: But before you go take a walk, grab a snack, or learn to meditate, there’s something much easier you can do right in this moment: get rid of distractions.
lines.zh: 不过在你动身去散步、去拿零食或者去学冥想之前，有一件更简单的事现在立刻就能做：清除干扰源。

lines.en: It’s impossible to remove every distraction, after all, our own wandering minds are often the biggest culprits.
lines.zh: 要把所有干扰都清除干净是不可能的，毕竟，我们自己那颗飘来飘去的心思往往才是最大的元凶。

lines.en: But one recent survey estimated that Americans now check their phones around 200 times a day.
lines.zh: 但是，最近一项调查估计，美国人现在每天要看大约 200 次手机。

lines.en: The distractions on our screens are designed to grab and hold attention.
lines.zh: 而屏幕上的那些干扰，是被专门设计出来抓取并留住注意力的。

lines.en: So, remember to be kind to yourself.
lines.zh: 所以，记得对自己宽容一些。

lines.en: While we can’t always control every factor that pulls at our attention, finding a quiet environment, closing extra tabs, and even blocking certain apps can give your brain the best chance at focusing in.
lines.zh: 虽然我们无法控制所有拉扯注意力的因素，但找一个安静的环境、关掉多余的标签页，甚至屏蔽某些应用，都能让你的大脑获得最好的专注机会。
